teaser: Have you ever wondered how to express being completely safe after a scary situation?
script: Welcome to Chengyu Bites — your quick summary on Chinese 成语. Have you ever wondered how to express being completely safe after a scary situation? [break 1s] The phrase is: 安然无恙, ānrán wúyàng. [break 1s] 安 (ān) - safe [break 0.5s] 然 (rán) - so, thus [break 0.5s] 无 (wú) - without [break 0.5s] 恙 (yàng) - harm, injury [break 1s] So, 安然无恙 literally means 'safe and sound' or 'without harm' and figuratively implies being unharmed after a dangerous experience. [break 1s] Here’s the story behind it: [break 1.5s] This idiom originates from the idea of someone returning from a perilous journey without any injuries or problems. In ancient times, travelers faced many dangers, and to arrive home safe and sound was a cause for celebration. It became a common phrase to express relief and joy when someone was unharmed. [break 1.5s] 例如，经过一场大风暴，他安然无恙。  After a fierce storm, he was safe and sound. [break 1s] 这次考试后，虽然我很紧张，但结果还是安然无恙。  After this exam, although I was very nervous, the result was still safe and sound. [break 1s] 她从车祸中幸存下来，真是安然无恙。  She survived the car accident; it’s truly a miracle she is unharmed. [break 1s] So, remember, 安然无恙 means safe and sound. Thank you for listening to Chengyu Bites! See you next time for another idiom. [break 1s]
